name: Mod

a recurring reference in British indie and Britpop styling
article: Mod began among young, working-class Londoners in the late 1950s who built an identity around things that were, for their time and class, genuinely difficult to access: Italian-cut suits, imported American soul and R&B singles, and motor scooters kept scrupulously clean. The name is short for "modernist," distinguishing the scene from the rougher 1950s Teddy Boy look it positioned itself against. Mod's visual signature — slim silhouettes, bold geometric color-blocking, the RAF roundel as an ironic badge — crossed into mainstream pop culture through bands like the Small Faces and, in a softened form, the Beatles, before a specifically British 1979 mod revival (tied to the film Quadrophenia) reintroduced the look to a new generation. Mod's emphasis on sharp, deliberate color combinations and clean geometry left a visible mark on later British design movements, from new wave's angular graphics to the mod-adjacent tailoring that's resurfaced periodically in Britpop and indie fashion ever since.
